shots.pre: The setting is Newgrange in the Boyne valley, Ireland, on the winter solstice morning, deep frost on the grass, hard cold, breath visible. Behind the people stands the great mound: a huge dome of earth and loose stones with grass on top, ringed by big grey kerbstones, white quartz and dark rounded cobbles scattered on the ground at its foot, a low dark passage entrance with a carved spiral stone lying in front of it. The sun is rising behind the camera; the camera looks at the people's faces. The people are Neolithic Irish farmers of 3200 BC: black hair, brown eyes, olive southern-European complexions, weathered skin. They wear tanned leather and deer-hide garments, fur capes, woven plant-fibre cloaks, leather foot wrappings, bone pins. No wool, no metal, no dyed cloth.

The setting is Stonehenge on the morning of the winter solstice today: thousands of people standing inside and around the circle of giant lichen-covered sarsen stones, frost on the grass, grey-violet sky turning pink, breath visible, hard cold. People wear puffer jackets, wool hats, scarves, gloves; a few wear white druid robes; some hold phones. The sun is rising behind the camera; the camera looks at their faces.
